titleEn: Law on Aggravating Circumstances of Crime

articles.en: - Purpose: this Law has the purpose of determining the aggravating circumstances of crimes in order to strengthen public security in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

-- Means of presenting evidence
1 - All witnesses named in the case file, including judicial police officers, must be allowed to speak before the court. A witness may be questioned and cross-examined by the civil party or his or her counsel, by the accused or his or her counsel, and by the public prosecutor.
2 - At the hearing, all evidence, including the records of judicial police officers, shall be put forward for debate and discussion, and such evidence and records of judicial police officers may not be treated as evidence that cannot be set aside.
3 - Confessions of accused persons that are not consistent with the origin of the evidence may not, in any case, be treated as a basis for conviction and punishment. A confession obtained by coercion or force of any kind shall be considered void; the request for such nullity shall be submitted to the judge by counsel for the accused before the judgment.
2238
4 - Counsel for the accused may bring his or her own witnesses before the court and may present his or her own evidence to the court.
5 - All witnesses, both for the prosecution and for the defence, may be compelled to appear before the court by summons of the court; in the event of failure to comply with the summons of the court, a fine from 50,000 (fifty thousand) riels to 500,000 (five hundred thousand) riels shall be imposed.

-- Premeditated murder
1 - Any person who kills or attempts to kill another person after having premeditated his or her crime, or who has prepared an ambush, or who kills or attempts to kill another person at the time when he or she commits robbery or rape, shall be guilty of the crime of premeditated murder and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 15 years to 20 years or for life.
2 - Premeditation is a plan formed before the act of aggression against any person.
An ambush is the lying in wait for a person over a period of time in order to commit an act of violence against that person.

-- Intentional homicide
Any person who intentionally kills a person or attempts to kill a person intentionally, without any of the aggravating circumstances provided in Article 3, whether or not a weapon was used, shall be guilty of the crime of intentional homicide and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 10 to 15 years.
Any person who intentionally kills a person with cruelty, in the same circumstances and in the same place, causing the death of one or several persons, shall be guilty of the crime of intentional homicide and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 15 years to 20 years or for life.
22349

-- Rape
1 - Any person who commits rape, or attempts to commit rape, on another person, whether of the same sex or not, shall be guilty of the crime of rape and shall be punished by imprisonment from 10 years to 15 years.
2 - Rape is any act of penetration of the sexual organ by any other means, committed with cruelty, by coercion, or against a person who is unaware in advance.
If the rape is committed with threats, by means of a weapon, against a pregnant woman, against a sick person or a person who has lost consciousness or is physically disabled, or against a minor under 14 years of age, committed by one or several perpetrators or by an accomplice, or if the sexual act is committed by a person who has authority over the victim, the penalty to be applied shall be imprisonment with compulsory labour from
15 years to 20 years.

-- Robbery. Robbery is the taking by deception and the extortion of the property of others, in any form, whether directly or indirectly, with the intention of making it one's own property.
Any person who steals, or attempts to steal, from another person with any of the following aggravating circumstances: - the theft is committed with violence, with or without a weapon, causing or not causing injury; - or the theft is committed by several persons, or by cutting, digging, climbing or damaging fences; shall be guilty of the crime of aggravated theft and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 5 years to 10 years.
- The theft committed with violence, with or without a weapon, causing the death of the owner, the victim, the family or a guardian or caretaker, shall be punishable as the crime of premeditated murder and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 15 years to
20 years or for life.
2240

-- Kidnapping and unlawful confinement of persons
1 - Any person who, without an order from the judicial authority, arrests, detains or confines any person shall be liable: - to imprisonment from 3 years to 5 years if the confinement lasts less than 1 month; - to imprisonment from 5 years to 10 years if the confinement or detention lasts more than 1 month.
2 - Any person who threatens in any form, by any means, in order to compel the handing over of money or property, with the intention of obtaining what he or she desires, shall be guilty of the crime of extortion and shall be punished by imprisonment from 5 years to 10 years.
3 - Any person who intentionally arrests one or several persons, takes them away to be detained or confined, or threatens to subject them to torture in any form, causing or not causing the death of any person, and threatens to compel a third person or the victim to hand over money, property or anything else in exchange for his or her own purposes, shall be guilty of the crime of kidnapping and unlawful confinement and shall be punished by imprisonment with compulsory labour from 15 years to 20 years or for life.

-- Mitigation and remission of penalties
In respect of felonies and misdemeanours punishable by imprisonment, the judge may not take into account any mitigating circumstance, nor reduce the penalty below the minimum, nor grant remission.
In respect of misdemeanours that do not seriously affect public order, the penalty may be remitted in whole or in part. In that case, the person who committed the offence shall not be subject to the full penalty if he or she does not commit another offence provided in the preceding articles within a period of 5 years after his or her conviction. 2244 Any provisions contrary to this Law shall be considered null and void.

This Law is promulgated as a matter of urgency.
Phnom Penh, [day and month illegible] 2012, in the Royal Name and in accordance with the Royal Command
